title: Console-binding constitution (T3 ref): the incidents that produced each Article
desc: Dated incident archive for exec-console-binding-constitution: the agy input-corruption trace, the same-day correction of Article 5, the wkinject counter-example, and the caller cascade as positive precedent. Core: exec-console-binding-constitution. Procedures: exec-console-binding-constitution-howto.
steps: INCIDENT: the measurement that produced the constitution, recorded so a successor re-derives it instead of re-suffering it. On 2026-08-20 the owner reported that running the installed agy through bin/agy.ps1 made his own typing unreliable and interfered with input in unrelated windows. The trace took four steps and each one is reusable. First, the reply rules fire through an injectStdin callback in RunCommand.Pty.OnMatch.cs, which is only a callback and therefore innocent. Second, PseudoConsoleRunner.cs line 223 starts a RelayInput thread whenever useFixedLargeSize is false, and RelayInput at line 370 polls Console.KeyAvailable every 20 milliseconds and calls Console.ReadKey with intercept true, which consumes the key so no other console client receives it. Third, the runner own comment at line 217 already explains why that thread is unsafe for automation callers and why it is skipped for the keystrokes-file case, which proves the omission of reply was an oversight rather than a decision. Fourth, RunCommand.cs line 261 takes the plain-pipe branch only when force-pty is absent, so force-pty combined with reply is the single route into the ConPTY branch carrying the narrow predicate, and bin/agy.ps1 uses exactly that shape with no keystrokes-file and no onexit. WHEN: any report that input is being eaten, or is arriving somewhere it was not aimed. HOW: trace the INPUT side rather than the output side, and run wkappbot skill read wkexec-conpty-keystrokes-ladder-ref for what has already been ruled out so the same ground is not re-walked. WHY: the symptom presents as a rendering or delivery problem while the cause was a lifecycle predicate two files away, so following the visible half would have consumed the entire investigation.

INCIDENT: THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE LESSON. Within the same hour of 2026-08-20 the constitution Article 5 was written as any automation flag proves no human is present, and the owner replied that a rule growing too broad is itself the defect. He was right and the article was wrong: a reply rule is REACTIVE and composes with a live human, since he types to agy himself while the rules auto-dismiss its approval prompts. Switching the console reader off, which is what the first draft implied and what a naive reading of the narrow predicate invites, would have taken his keyboard away entirely. The corrected split is by EVIDENCE rather than by flag -- keystrokes-file and onexit are fully scripted and do prove absence, while reply proves nothing about presence -- and the real hazard turned out to be ARBITRATION rather than existence: five call sites write the one ConPTY input handle with no mutual exclusion, so a reply firing mid-keystroke splices into the human line. WHEN: any moment a fix looks like one line in a predicate. HOW: ask what the flag actually MEANS to a user before treating its presence as proof of anything, and run wkappbot skill read exec-console-binding-constitution to check the proposed rule against Article 4 and Article 5 as they now stand. WHY: the obvious fix here was actively harmful, and the only thing that caught it was describing the intended change to the owner in plain language before shipping it.

INCIDENT: REPAIRED 2026-09-20 FOR THE wkinject.exe AUTO PATH (kih 3ffc9c8d6): the no-pid target is accepted only when GetConsoleProcessList of its own console lists it, otherwise exit 2 naming Article 2 or 4; explicit --pid or --pname outside the own console still works but is confessed on stderr; callers name the launching session through Get-WkAiAncestorPid. NOT REPAIRED: the AiConsoleInjector.TryConInInject walk described below (a separate resolver, unchecked), and callers still select the AI ancestor by image name plus parent lineage rather than by a proved console. THE PRIOR ART IS ALSO THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE -- wkinject, the console injector that predates the PTY responder, violates the constitution in three places, and reading it is the fastest way to understand why the Articles are shaped as they are. WHAT IT DOES, in AiConsoleInjector.TryConInInject: resolve a leaf PID from an HWND, walk up to EIGHT ancestor levels, collect any ancestor whose process NAME appears in a hardcoded list of cmd, conhost, OpenConsole, WindowsTerminal, pwsh and powershell, take the FIRST match, and if nothing matches but the window class is CASCADIA then fall back to using the LEAF PID itself as a last-resort host -- then FreeConsole, AttachConsole onto that host, open CONIN and WriteConsoleInput. THE THREE VIOLATIONS. Against Article 2 it selects by NAME rather than by proved ownership, so with two terminal windows open the walk simply finds a terminal. Against Article 10 an eight-level ancestor walk in a shell tree reliably reaches the terminal host that every tab shares, a broad signal used as a selector. Against Article 4, and this is the dangerous one, a failed resolution does not refuse but GUESSES the leaf and injects anyway, which is fail-open at the exact moment the code has admitted it does not know where it is aiming. AND THE API SHAPE ITSELF: FreeConsole followed by AttachConsole onto another process is literally abandoning your own console to enter somebody else, and if the restoring AttachConsole with ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS then fails, the process is left attached to a foreign console with no indication. WHEN: before writing any new console-targeting code, and when investigating any keystroke that arrived in the wrong place. HOW: read this resolver first and treat it as the list of things not to repeat, and run wkappbot skill read wkinject-focusless-console-keystroke-injector-exe for what the tool promises versus what it does. WHY: a predecessor session ran this injector with no explicit pid, the owner next message was a bare digit 1, and that session retired without ever establishing where the keystroke landed -- the last-resort leaf fallback is the mechanism that makes such a stray injection possible, and it was in the code the whole time.

VERIFIED: THE CALLER CASCADE IS THE POSITIVE PRECEDENT, AND THE CONSTITUTION IS ITS CODIFICATION RATHER THAN AN INVENTION. The owner observed on 2026-08-20 that AppBot has suffered over finding the right caller window since its earliest days. Reading that cascade against the Articles shows it already obeys them: an environment override first is the embedded-host rule, because inside a terminal host the parent chain is not trustworthy; a WT_SESSION-matched terminal is the two-axes rule, corroborating the window axis rather than replacing it; and ending at Zero rather than at a best guess is the fail-closed rule in its purest form, with the skill stating that Zero outcome as CORRECT rather than as a gap. THE PROPERTY UNDER THREAT is that last one, because a Zero return looks like a bug to anyone who has not read why it is there. WHEN: any change to caller-HWND resolution, window placement, or IPC caller identity, and any report that placement did not happen. HOW: treat the cascade as the reference implementation instead of re-deriving a heuristic, and run wkappbot skill read eye-ipc-caller-hwnd-resolution for the cascade itself. WHY: two subsystems in one product face the identical question, which one process among many is mine -- the caller path answers with layered evidence and a refusal at the end, the injector answers with a name match and a last-resort guess, and only the first has never put a keystroke somewhere nobody could account for.

TODO: give the Chrome placement rectangle a single owner and restore the Zero-means-skip refusal that step 4 records as the positive precedent, because the placement paths currently violate the very cascade this skill holds up as the reference implementation. WHEN: the owner reports Chrome windows landing too small, jumping to a screen corner, or overlapping the caller wrongly, or any work begins on window placement or sizing. HOW: run wkappbot skill read exec-console-binding-constitution for Articles 1, 3 and 4, then read csharp/src/WKAppBot.WebBot/CdpClient.Window2.cs lines 25-110 where OuterWidthPx 804 and OuterHeightPx 710 are hardcoded, and csharp/src/WKAppBot.WebBot/CallerPlacementResolver.cs line 302 where ComputePlacementNearWindow takes the caller HANDLE but receives width and height AS ARGUMENTS -- the caller rect drives POSITION ONLY and size arrives pre-decided, so there is no structural path for a caller-size floor to exist; then check ChromeLauncher.Placement.cs lines 20, 90 and 123, whose own comments admit they fall back to ExpectedBounds at the legacy 40,40 or 1740,20 anchor far from the caller when the caller latch is cleared. WHY: measured 2026-08-24 while answering the owner directly. He asked why the browser window is mostly too small and described the design he wants -- Chrome and the caller OVERLAPPING but offset so he can click the upper-left or the lower-right to focus whichever he means. The offset half already exists as ChromeLauncher.CallerPlacementOffset at minus 30 by minus 30, so only the size and the refusal are missing. SIX independent mechanisms can move a Chrome window and each computes its own rectangle, so a floor added at any one site is overwritten by the other five -- the single owner must land BEFORE the one-line max against the caller rect, or the fix will not hold. TWO TRAPS. FIRST, Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride pins the render viewport to 800 by 600 after every CDP connection explicitly regardless of outer window size, so raising the window without releasing that pin grows the frame while the page stays small, and prompt injection plus screenshot capture may compute coordinates against that fixed viewport. SECOND, DPI is handled four different ways on the same rectangle: two paths multiply by dpi over 96 while ChromeLauncher.LaunchWindow.cs line 20 states in the past tense that scaling there DOUBLE-SCALES the size, and CdpClient.Window2.cs line 273 accepts roughly 14 pixels of drift as tolerance, which is two computations disagreeing rather than a rounding allowance. This is Article 14 territory and belongs to an Opus agent per the global DPI rule. Full audit with file and line for every claim: .tmp/evidence/chrome-resize-audit-2026-08-24.md. Cross: standard-appbot-window step 3, standard-chrome-window, caller-window-rect-dpi-piping-ipc-extension-for-precise-chrome-placement.
